---
title: "11. Remote computing"
---

```{r, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
library(dMod2)
# the local job runs in an empty folder, where it finds no shared objects of other articles
.work <- tempfile("remote-computing-")
dir.create(.work)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = .work)
.outdir <- options(dMod2.outdir = NULL)
```

dMod2 uses cores along two axes. The conditions of one objective evaluation are solved in threads
of one process; independent fits and profiles run as processes of their own.
`distributedComputing()` takes the second axis beyond the R session: it runs any R code as tasks
in processes detached from the session, on the local machine, on machines reached by ssh or as an
array job of a SLURM cluster. This chapter sums up the two axes, runs a job of general R code on
the local machine, describes what `distributedComputing()` does with it, and ends with the fits
and profiles of the guide project on a cluster. The local job runs when this page is built; the
commands for other machines are shown, not run.

## Threads and processes

One evaluation of the objective `obj` solves the ODE of every condition with its sensitivities.
`options(dMod2.cores = n)`, or `obj(pars, cores = n)` for a single call, solves the conditions in
`n` threads inside the C++ code. The model of the guide has two conditions, so two threads are the
most this axis uses; a model with many conditions, or `em()` with many groups, gains in
proportion.

Independent fits share nothing but the model, so they run as processes forked from the session.
`mstrust()`, `msem()` and `profile()` take `cores` for this axis, and
`cores = c(fits = 4, conditions = 2)` runs four fits at a time with two threads each. Every forked
fit holds its own predictions, so the process axis multiplies the memory, while threads share one
process. The product of the two should stay below the number of cores.

| where | argument | axis |
|---|---|---|
| one evaluation | `options(dMod2.cores = )`, `obj(pars, cores = )` | conditions, threads |
| `em()` | `cores` | groups and conditions, threads |
| `mstrust()`, `msem()` | `cores`, or `c(fits = , conditions = )` | fits, processes |
| `profile()` | `cores`, or `c(pars = , conditions = )` | profiled parameters, processes |
| `distributedComputing()` | `tasks`, `on` | tasks, detached processes on this or other machines |

```{r}
options(dMod2.cores = 2)
fits <- mstrust(obj, mu[free], fixed = gauge, sd = 2, fits = 20,
                cores = c(fits = 4, conditions = 2))
profiles <- profile(obj, best, names(best), fixed = gauge, cores = 8)
```

## Tasks

`distributedComputing(expr, tasks, on)` evaluates the R code `expr` once per task, each time in a
fresh R process, and the value of `expr` is the result of the task. `tasks` is a number of tasks,
a list or vector with one element per task, or a data frame with one row per task. In the code

- `task` is the element or row of the task, a row as a list (`task$n`), and `NULL` when `tasks`
  is a number,
- `taskId` is its position in `tasks`,
- `cores` is the number of cores the task may use, which parallel code takes as it is, such as
  `mstrust(cores = cores)`, `parallel::mclapply(mc.cores = cores)` or
  `options(dMod2.cores = cores)`,
- `jobname` is the name of the job.

`input` names the objects of the session that the code reads, by default every object of the
calling environment; functions are objects like any other. The process attaches dMod2 besides
the default packages of R: the code loads other packages itself, and the options of the session,
`dMod2.cores` among them, do not reach it.

As an example of general R code, the coverage of the 95% t interval for the mean of exponential
samples, one task per sample size, as a job on the local machine:

```{r coverage, eval = TRUE}
interval <- function(y) t.test(y)$conf.int
sizes <- data.frame(n = c(5, 10, 20, 50))
job <- distributedComputing(
  {
    message("task ", taskId, ": samples of size ", task$n)
    covered <- replicate(2000, {
      ci <- interval(rexp(task$n))
      ci[1] < 1 && 1 < ci[2]
    })
    data.frame(n = task$n, coverage = mean(covered))
  },
  tasks = sizes, on = localNode(cores = 1), jobname = "coverage", input = "interval", seed = 1
)
job
```

The call returns once the tasks have started, and the session stays free. `job` is a list of
functions that follow the job: `check()` reports the state of its tasks, `wait()` polls until none
runs, and `get()` joins the results, here the data frames of the tasks into one.

```{r follow, eval = TRUE}
job$check()
job$wait(interval = 1)
job$get()
```

Task `i` starts with the seed `seed + i`, so its result does not depend on the worker it runs on or
on the order of the tasks; without `seed`, `distributedComputing()` draws one. A task whose code
raises an error has the error as its result, a `try-error`, and the other tasks go on.

## Job folder

At the submission `distributedComputing()` writes the files of the job into a temporary stage and
copies the stage to every node, as one `tar` stream through ssh, into the folder
`<jobname>_folder/<k>` of the home directory, `k` the number of the node. On `"localhost"` the
folder lies in the working directory, and the copy goes without ssh. The local `<jobname>_folder`
also holds `job.rds`, the manifest of the job. After the run of the local job:

```{r folder, eval = TRUE}
list.files("coverage_folder", recursive = TRUE)
```

| file | content |
|---|---|
| `workspace.RData` | the objects of `input`, saved by `save()`; compressed with `zstd` when the local machine has it, and unpacked on the node |
| `tasks.rds` | the tasks as a list, a data frame as one list per row |
| `job.R` | the R script of a task |
| model files | sources, object files or shared objects of the models, see [Model files and builds](#model-files-and-builds) |
| `build.sh`, `files.txt`, `build.log` | the build of the model files on the node, and its output |
| `slot_<k>.sh`, `slot_<k>.pid`, `slot_<k>.run` | the script that runs the tasks of node `k`, its process ID, and that of the running task |
| `job.sh`, `env.sh` | on a SLURM cluster: the job script filled in from the template, and its environment |
| `task_<i>.out`, `task_<i>.rds` | the output and the result of task `i` |

`job.R` is the same for every task, which comes from the command line,
`Rscript job.R <taskId> <cores>`, with the output in `task_<taskId>.out`:

```{r jobscript, eval = TRUE}
writeLines(readLines("coverage_folder/1/job.R"))
```

It attaches dMod2, loads the workspace and the shared objects of the folder, reads its task from
`tasks.rds`, sets the seed and evaluates the code inside `try()`. The result goes to
`task_<taskId>.rds`, which `get()` reads. Each task is a process of its own, so nothing passes from
one task to the next but files. The code runs in the job folder of its node: files it writes land
there, and `get(all = TRUE)` copies them back.

## Nodes and workers

`on` says where the tasks run:

```{r}
on <- localNode()                                        # the local machine, its free cores
on <- localNode(cores = 8)
on <- sshNodes(c("server1", "server2"))                  # each node with its free cores
on <- sshNodes(c("server1", "server2"), cores = 10)
on <- sshNodes(cores = c(server1 = 24, server2 = 20))
on <- sshNodes(c("localhost", "server1"))                # the local machine and one more
on <- slurmCluster("mycluster", cores = 8, walltime = "12:00:00")
```

A node is an ssh destination such as `"host"` or `"user@host"`, reached with key authentication,
since the commands run without a terminal to type a password in. The name `"localhost"` is the
local machine, reached without ssh: its commands run in the shell of the session, in the working
directory, and its tasks in the R and with the library paths of the session. A job on the local
machine needs neither ssh nor a second installation of dMod2; `localNode()` is
`sshNodes("localhost")`.

The tasks run on workers, and a node is one worker. The tasks are dealt to the workers in turn,
task `i` to worker `(i - 1) %% W + 1` of `W`, and a worker runs its tasks one after the other, each
with the `cores` of its node. On two nodes two tasks run at a time, and the parallel code inside a
task uses the cores of its node. `tasks = NULL`, the default, gives one task per worker.

`cores` is the number of cores of each task on a node: one number for all nodes, a vector named by
node, or `NULL` for the free cores at the submission. `detectFreeCores()` counts them as the cores
of a machine minus its load average of the last minute, at least 1, on the local machine or
through ssh; a node gets at most its free cores, with a warning when it was given more.

```{r}
detectFreeCores(c("localhost", "server1", "server2"))
```

On each node the tasks run in the shell script `slot_<k>.sh`, which calls `Rscript job.R` for every
task of the node in turn. It is started as `nohup setsid sh slot_<k>.sh &`: `setsid` gives it a
session of its own and `nohup` shields it from the hangup signal, so it runs on when the ssh
connection or the R session ends. The tasks run with `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` and `MKL_NUM_THREADS=1`,
so that BLAS and OpenMP start no threads beyond those the code asks for, and with the library paths
of `libs` first.

## Model files and builds

A model object calls compiled code, which has to be on the node. The model files of a job are those
of the model objects in `input`, the `obsfn`, `parfn`, `prdfn` and objectives, found through the
sources they were generated from; objects without them take every model file of
`getOption("dMod2.outdir")`, else of the working directory. `build` says how they reach the nodes:

- `"compile"`: the C and C++ sources are copied, and `build.sh` compiles them on each node into one
  shared object, against the cppDE installed there: with its headers, its SUNDIALS and KLU, the
  `-D` switches of the model and `-O2`. It runs `buildCores` compilers at a time, by default the
  cores of the node, at most 16. Past the length limit of a command line the objects go through a
  static archive, with `buildBundle` sources per translation unit.
- `"link"`: the object files are copied and linked on each node, which needs a compiler there
  compatible with the local one.
- `"copy"`: the shared objects are copied, which needs a node compatible with the local machine.
- `"auto"`, the default: `"copy"` when every node is `"localhost"`, `"compile"` otherwise.

The build runs once per node, before the first task: the tasks of a node share its folder and load
the one shared object, to which `job.R` points every model object of the workspace
(`modelname()`). On a SLURM cluster the build runs once on the login node for all array
tasks. Its output goes to `build.log` in the job folder; a failed build stops the submission, and
the error shows the end of the log. `libs` puts library paths first on the nodes, for the build
and the tasks; the remote shell expands them, so `~` is the remote home.

The coverage job has no model files: `input` holds no model object, and the working directory no
shared object.

## Following a job

| function | does |
|---|---|
| `check()` | prints how many tasks are done, running and failed; returns `TRUE` once none runs, with a warning when some failed |
| `wait(interval = 10)` | polls every `interval` seconds until no task runs, reports each change, and returns `TRUE` when every task is done |
| `get(combine = TRUE, all = FALSE)` | returns the results |
| `log(i, lines = 20)` | prints the last lines of the output of task `i` |
| `purge(local = FALSE)` | deletes the job folders on the nodes, with `local = TRUE` also the local one and the registry entry |
| `terminate()` | stops the tasks |

A task is done when its result file exists, running while its worker runs, also when it waits for
its turn, and failed when its worker has ended without its result. `get()` copies the result files
of remote nodes through ssh into the local `<jobname>_folder/<k>`, with `all = TRUE` every file of
the job folders. It joins parlists with `c()` and data frames, parameter frames among them, with
`rbind()`, which also joins the two sides of a profile into one; other results come as a list.
Tasks without a result are left out with a warning. `get(combine = FALSE)` returns one entry per
task, named like `tasks`: `NULL` for a task not done, the `try-error` of a failed one.
`terminate()` ends the process group of every slot, on a SLURM cluster the job by `scancel`.

The output of the second task, and the deletion of the job:

```{r purge, eval = TRUE}
job$log(2)
job$purge(local = TRUE)
```

`distributedComputing(wait = TRUE)` waits for the tasks itself, returns the result of `get()` and
deletes the job; a job with failed tasks is kept, and `log()` shows their output.

A job outlives the session that submitted it. Its manifest lies in the local `<jobname>_folder`, in
the folder of every remote node, and in the registry of jobs, `tools::R_user_dir("dMod2", "data")`,
until `purge(local = TRUE)`; `dMod2Jobs()` lists the registered jobs. `recover = TRUE` with the
name of a job returns its functions without submitting it again: from the manifest in the working
directory, else from the registry, else, with `on` given, from the folder on its remote nodes,
which recovers a job submitted from another machine. A new job of the same name is an error while
the old one still runs where the new one would replace its folders: in the same working directory,
or on the same remote nodes, also when it was submitted from another machine.

```{r}
dMod2Jobs()
job <- distributedComputing(jobname = "fits", recover = TRUE)
job <- distributedComputing(jobname = "fits", on = sshNodes(c("server1", "server2")),
                            recover = TRUE)
```

## SLURM clusters

`slurmCluster()` names the login node of a cluster, reached by ssh, and the resources of one array
task: `cores`, `walltime` and `memPerCore` in GB. The workers are the array tasks, `array` of them,
by default one per task; array task `j` runs the tasks `j`, `j + array`, `j + 2 * array`, ... one
after the other. The stage goes to `~/<jobname>_folder/1` on the login node. There the environment
of the template is set up, the model files are built once, and `sbatch` submits the array job from
that folder, so the compute nodes have to see the home directory of the login node, as on most
clusters. `partition`, `account`, `maxRunning` (the most array tasks at once) and `sbatch` (further
options, such as `"--constraint=ib"`) go to `sbatch` and take precedence over the `#SBATCH` lines
of the template. The start reports the job ID; `check()` reads the state from `squeue`, and
`terminate()` calls `scancel`.

The job script comes from a template, set up once per login node with `slurmTemplate()` and kept in
`tools::R_user_dir("dMod2", "config")`. A template is a job script of the cluster with the
placeholders `{{ jobname }}`, `{{ ntasks }}` (the number of array tasks), `{{ cores }}`,
`{{ memPerCore }}` and `{{ walltime }}`, and one line `{{ run }}`, which runs the tasks of the array
task. The lines before `{{ run }}` that are not comments set up the environment, for example with
`module load`; the build on the login node runs in it too. A placeholder without a value is an
error, so a template with `{{ walltime }}` needs `walltime`. The template dMod2 ships for the
bwForCluster Helix:

```{r template, eval = TRUE}
writeLines(readLines(system.file("slurm", "helix.sh", package = "dMod2")))
```

```{r}
slurmTemplate("mycluster", from = "~/mycluster.sh")   # once, from a job script, for editing
slurmTemplate("helix")                                 # the template dMod2 ships for Helix
slurmTemplate()                                        # the templates set up
cluster <- slurmCluster("helix", cores = 1, walltime = "12:00:00")
```

`slurmCluster(jobscript = )` takes another template for a single job.

## Fits and profiles of the guide project

The 500 fits of `fit.R` from [chapter 4](guide-optimization.html), as 500 tasks of one fit on one
core, each from the start that its own seed draws:

```{r}
free <- setdiff(names(mu), names(gauge))
fitsJob <- distributedComputing(
  mstrust(obj, mu[free], fixed = gauge, sd = 2, fits = 1, iterlim = 1000, tolControl = tolerances),
  tasks = 500, on = cluster, jobname = "oppelt_fits", seed = 1,
  input = c("obj", "mu", "free", "gauge", "tolerances"))
fitsJob$check()
fitsJob$wait(interval = 60)
fits <- as.parframe(fitsJob$get())
fitsJob$purge(local = TRUE)
```

The sources of `obj` are compiled once on the login node, and every task loads `obj` and fits.
`get()` joins the parlists of the tasks, and `as.parframe()` sorts the fits by value. A session
started later, also on another day, takes up the job by its name:

```{r}
fitsJob <- distributedComputing(jobname = "oppelt_fits", recover = TRUE)
```

The profiles of [chapter 5](guide-profiles.html), one side of one parameter per task, from a data
frame of tasks:

```{r}
sides <- expand.grid(par = names(bestWide), side = c("left", "right"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
profilesJob <- distributedComputing(
  profile(objWide, bestWide, task$par, side = task$side, fixed = gauge,
          limits = c(lower = -7, upper = 7), stepControl = list(stop = "data"),
          algoControl = list(reoptimize = TRUE),
          optControl = list(iterlim = 100, tolControl = tolerances)),
  tasks = sides, on = cluster, jobname = "oppelt_profiles",
  input = c("objWide", "bestWide", "gauge", "tolerances"))
profilesJob$wait(interval = 60)
profiles <- profilesJob$get()
```

`get()` binds the parameter frames of the tasks, the two sides of a parameter into one profile.

On machines without SLURM as many tasks run at a time as there are nodes, each with the cores of
its node. One task per node, the default of `tasks`, with ten fits per core of the node:

```{r}
fitsJob <- distributedComputing(
  mstrust(obj, mu[free], fixed = gauge, sd = 2, fits = 10 * cores, iterlim = 1000,
          tolControl = tolerances, cores = cores),
  on = sshNodes(c("server1", "server2")), jobname = "oppelt_fits", seed = 1,
  input = c("obj", "mu", "free", "gauge", "tolerances"))
```

[Bile acid transport](bileAcidTransport.html) runs its multistarts as a job on the local machine,
[Kok 2020](kokMSB2020.html) its 200 fits as an array job on Helix.

## Requirements

The local machine runs the commands of a job in a POSIX shell, on Windows in the `sh` of Rtools,
and every remote node needs one. A remote node is reached by ssh with key authentication and has
dMod2 and cppDE installed for the R on its path, or in `libs`; `build = "compile"` also needs a
compiler there. A SLURM cluster needs an account on its login node, a template set up with
`slurmTemplate()`, and a home directory that the compute nodes see. `zstd`, when the local machine
has it, compresses the workspace and is then needed on every remote node.

## Summary

- Many conditions: `options(dMod2.cores = )` or `em(cores = )`, threads inside one evaluation.
- Many fits or profiles in the session: `cores` of `mstrust()`, `msem()` and `profile()`, forked
  processes.
- Any R code as tasks detached from the session: `distributedComputing()` on `localNode()`,
  `sshNodes()` or `slurmCluster()`, followed by `check()`, `wait()`, `get()` and `purge()`, and
  taken up again with `recover = TRUE`.

```{r, include = FALSE, eval = TRUE, purl = FALSE}
options(.outdir)
```
